themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints spiked to 4 THIS WEEK versus a baseline average of 1.2 per week (220% increase, z-score 4.16), suggesting a sudden surge in Uber/Lyft traffic or driver behavior issues in Mott Haven/Melrose that warrants immediate investigation.
evidence: 4 for-hire vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
z-score of 4.16 indicates statistically significant spike
220% increase represents one of the newest and most acute spikes in the dataset
reporting_angles: Interview residents and local businesses about specific complaints (illegal parking, blocking lanes, driver behavior); obtain 311 complaint details
Reach out to TLC and for-hire vehicle companies for data on increased pickups/dropoffs in the district; investigate any surge in app-based rides

themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retailer Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints jumped to 4 TWO WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 0.2 per week (1500% spike, z-score 8.66—the highest in the dataset), indicating a potential new dispensary, illegal operation, or neighborhood opposition that has not yet faded.
evidence: 4 cannabis retailer complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
z-score of 8.66 is the single highest statistical anomaly in entire dataset
1500% increase represents an unprecedented spike in this complaint category for the district
reporting_angles: Identify which new dispensaries opened in CD 201 in the past 2-3 weeks; map locations and interview neighbors about specific complaints (odor, loitering, sales practices)
Contact NYC Office of Cannabis Management for licensing status; investigate any unlicensed operations or SLA violations; speak with local precinct on enforcement

themes_detail.label: Missed Garbage Collections Spike
themes_detail.summary: Missed collection complaints surged to 7 LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 1.1 per week (522% increase, z-score 3.64), suggesting a potential sanitation service failure or staffing issue affecting waste pickup across the neighborhood.
evidence: 7 missed collection complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
z-score of 3.64 indicates statistically significant deviation
522% increase coincides with related street sweeping spike (6 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.0 avg, z-score 3.54)
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Sanitation (DSNY) to determine if there were service disruptions, crew shortages, or route changes in CD 201 last week
Document specific blocks or neighborhoods most affected; interview residents about collection delays and hygiene/pest impacts; tie to broader sanitation staffing trends

themes_detail.label: Non-Emergency Police Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police matter complaints jumped to 16 LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 5.8 per week (178% increase, z-score 4.61), indicating either a surge in low-level crime, quality-of-life complaints, or police response issues warranting closer examination.
evidence: 16 non-emergency police complaints LAST WEEK vs. 5.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
z-score of 4.61 places this among the top statistical anomalies
178% increase may correlate with encampment spike (12 complaints 3 weeks ago, z-score 4.47) and park noise spike (4 complaints last week, z-score 3.4)
reporting_angles: Obtain detailed 311 complaint logs to identify specific incident types (trespassing, loitering, disturbance); contact 44th Precinct for crime and quality-of-life data
Investigate whether spike is driven by homelessness/encampments, street disorder, or other root causes; interview residents and police on enforcement trends

themes_detail.label: Homelessness & Encampment Crisis Signals
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints spiked to 12 THREE WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 2.0 per week (500% increase, z-score 4.47), coupled with elevated non-emergency police calls and park noise complaints, suggesting visible homelessness and associated public safety/quality-of-life strain.
evidence: 12 encampment complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 2.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
z-score of 4.47 indicates major statistical spike
Converges with non-emergency police spike (16 complaints last week) and park noise spike (4 last week), suggesting interconnected homelessness/disorder issue
Community Board budget requests repeatedly cite homelessness services as unfunded priority
reporting_angles: Map locations of recent encampments using 311 data; conduct street reporting on visible camps in parks and public spaces; interview unhoused residents about needs
Contact NYC Department of Homeless Services on outreach capacity and shelter placement in/near CD 201; examine any connection to shelter capacity crisis citywide
